extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and KIPO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for converted applications and priority claims under the Korean Patent Act (Article 54) and related KIPO examination practice; guidance for filing, amendment, documentation, and examination. Targets applicants, successors, and examiners handling Korean national filings asserting foreign priority or converted/divisional filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant after notice for inadmissible conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible for the examiner to decide to grant a patent after the service of notice for inadmissible conversion if there is no ground for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if conversion was deemed inadmissible, examiner may still grant where substantive examination shows no grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and rejection for inventions not described in original (post-2006 filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a converted application was filed for an invention not described in the original application, the examiner shall notify the applicant of the ground for rejection; if the applicant cannot address the ground even with written arguments or amendments, the examiner shall decide to reject the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where the original application was filed on or after October 1, 2006; examiner must give notice and allow response before rejecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment period for converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The period allowed for amendments to the specification or drawing(s) of a converted application is within the period prescribed in the subparagraphs of Article 47(1) of the Patent Act, retroactively counted from the filing date of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive counting: the amendment window is measured from the original application's filing date per Article 47(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application examined as ordinary application when requirements fulfilled
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a converted application fulfills the procedural and substantive requirements, the examiner shall regard the converted application as an ordinary application and examine its legality on amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original specification/drawings of the converted application serve as the specification/drawings with which substantive requirements on the amendment are examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on addition of new subject matter in converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention not contained in the original specification of the converted application is newly added through amendments after filing the converted application, the examiner shall examine the application in accordance with the requirements of prohibiting the addition of new subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies where an invention is described in the original application but not in the spec/drawings of the converted application; strict new-matter rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional-based converted application allowed but not within single patent procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can file a converted application by taking a divisional application as the original application. However, the converted application shall not be deemed to be legitimate if division and conversion of an application are carried out in the single patent procedure, such as converting a part of a patent application to a utility model registration application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If intending to convert a part to another type, file a divisional first in the same form, then file the converted application based on the divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of converted application when filed with reexamination/appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files a converted application along with making a request for reexamination regarding the rejected application or making an appeal against the decision to reject the application, the examiner shall accept the application if the procedure for the application is legitimate in terms of the formalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a request for examination is made for the converted application, the examiner shall conduct the examination. For reexamination/appeal, the original application is deemed withdrawn under Article 53(4) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date when original was pending then returned after conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original application was pending before KIPO at the time of filing a converted application, but was returned after the conversion of the application, the examiner shall examine the converted application based on the date when it was actually filed, not giving the same filing date of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If converted application has grounds for rejection, examiner shall notify the applicant why it cannot take the retroactive filing date plus grounds for rejection; if no rejection grounds, notify via On-nara system why retroactive date not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted application cannot be based on multiple original applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A converted application shall not be filed based on multiple original applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: it may be possible to file a converted application after an application claiming Domestic Priority has been filed on the basis of two or more prior-filed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on filing converted application after certified copy of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If thirty days have elapsed from the date when an applicant received a certified copy of the initial decision to reject, the applicant shall not file a converted application if the decision to reject was cancelled through a request for reexamination or a trial decision or if thirty days have not elapsed from the date when a certified copy of the decision to reject was delivered again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of the decision to reject through reexamination does not necessarily nullify the fact that a certified copy of the initial decision to reject was delivered for the first time; timing rules are strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 54(1) priority recognition under treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable under a treaty, the filing date of a patent application in the contracting state of the treaty shall be deemed the filing date of the patent application in the Republic of Korea for purposes of Article 29 or 36.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets cross-border recognition of filing date when treaty conditions satisfied (Paris Convention/TRIPS/bilateral treaties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file Korean application claiming priority (one year)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to claim priority under paragraph (1) shall file a patent application within one year from the filing date of the first application which forms the basis of the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Paris Convention one-year rule for patent/utility-model priority claims; see also six-month rule for designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statement of intention and first application details
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to claim priority shall state in the patent application his/her intention, the name of the state in which the first application was filed, and the filing date of the first application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the priority claim explicit in the written application (Article 4D(5) of Paris Convention referred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of evidential documents or written statement for priority (Article 54(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who claims priority shall submit certified copies of the specification and drawings of the relevant invention certified by the government of the state in which the first application was filed, or a written statement specifying details (only for states specified by Ordinance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written-statement option is limited to states specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy; certified copies are the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for submitting evidential documents (one year and four months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents or written statements referred to must be submitted within one year and four months from the earliest among specified dates (filing date of first application; filing date of application on which priority claim is based where Article 55(1) applies; filing date where claim under paragraph (3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit within this period causes the priority claim to become void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend/add priority within one year and four months
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who claims priority and meets the requirements may amend or add a priority claim within one year and four months from the earliest date specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the window for correcting or adding priority claims (including multiple priority claims containing Domestic Priority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is eligible to make a priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A person eligible is a national of a contracting state of the treaty or a national of a non-contracting state who has a domicile or a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in a contracting state; where multiple applicants, at least one must meet this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting states include Paris Convention/WTO members; EPO/EAPO/OAPI/ARIPO signatories considered contracting states for purposes of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim only after first application filed in contracting state
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim can be made only after an application was filed in a contracting state of the treaty (the country where it was firstly filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inventor granted the right to file to another person and did not file the first application, the inventor cannot make a priority claim based on that first application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability of right to subsequent filings (succession)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to make any subsequent filing in any of the other countries of the Treaty can be transferred to other successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successor must meet nationality/domicile criteria at relevant times (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor eligibility for priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The successor eligible for filing an application claiming a priority shall be a national of a contracting state of the treaty both at the time of filing the first application and at the time of filing any subsequent application; however, the requirement need not be met during the intervening period between filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a successor becomes a national of a contracting state before subsequent filing, succession of the right is valid. Transfers to/from nationals of non-contracting states with domicile in contracting states are also addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of first application that may form basis for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The first application filed in one of the countries under the Treaty shall be one of the following applications: a patent application, an application for utility model registration or design registration or an inventor’s certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, due to characteristics, an application for design registration or a service mark shall not be recognized as a basis for a patent application claiming a priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity of first application not affected by later status
rubrics_metrics.description: The first application filed must be regular as determined by the relevant law of the country; whether the first application is pending does not influence the effects of the priority claim—even if withdrawn, abandoned, invalidated or rejected, priority claim remains effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the first application later fails to produce a patent in its country, priority effects under the Convention persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earliest-application requirement for priority basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The first application shall be the earliest application or an application to be recognized as the earliest-filed application; priority cannot be claimed on an application that is not the earliest for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: you cannot claim priority to a March filing if a May filing was actually an earlier applicable filing for the same invention; the earliest-filed rule is strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for a subsequent application to be recognized as the earliest
rubrics_metrics.description: For a subsequent application to be recognized as the earliest application, it must: (①) be filed for the same invention in the same country where the previous first application was filed; (②) the previous first application must be withdrawn/abandoned/rejected before the subsequent application is filed; (③) the previous first application must not be published; (④) no rights shall be effective because of the previous first application; (⑤) the previous first application shall not serve as a basis for a priority claim in the same or different countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All five requirements must be fulfilled to treat the subsequent application as the earliest for priority purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of written patent application for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to make a priority claim shall write the purport of the priority claim and the country name as well as the filing date of the first application in a written patent application; the first application number which forms a basis for a priority claim shall be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments related to making the priority claim must also be made upon making the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of evidential documents within one year and four months
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who has made a priority claim shall submit to the Commissioner of KIPO the documents containing the application date recognized by the government of the country where the first application was filed as well as the copy of the specification or drawing(s) within one year and four months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In countries designated in the Enforcement Decree, submission may be replaced by submitting application numbers; failure to submit within the period causes loss of priority effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined procedures: countries and DAS/EPO/USPTO specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries with streamlined procedures (e.g., Japan, EPC signatories, DAS-access countries) allow replacing evidential documents with application numbers; only EPO replacement works for EPC signatories; USPTO provides documents only under written authorization (PTO/SB/39); DAS-access relies on application numbers and advance DAS access requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an applicant's filing country falls into the streamlined list is determined based on the filing date of the application in the Republic of Korea; specific cut-off dates for Japan, EPC, USPTO/DAS access are given in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple priority claims mixing streamlined and non-streamlined countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple priority claims are made based on both an application filed in a country with a streamlined procedure and an application filed in a country without it, only the evidential documents for the streamlined-country claim can be replaced by the application number; evidential documents for the other claims must be submitted by existing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow mixed submission requirements when claims span different categories of countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require Korean translation of evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner requires the applicant to submit the Korean translation of the evidential documents claiming a priority within the designated time period in order to determine patentability (e.g., when prior art exists between priority and filing date), the applicant shall submit the Korean translation within the designated time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed period is two months, extendable. Failure to submit translation may invalidate the proceedings for the concerned priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations treated as reference material; amendments allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the translation of the evidential documents certifying the priority is just a reference material for proving the priority claim, amendments to the translation shall be deemed to be valid, even with substantial changes in the contents of the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation is not the controlling original; substantive changes in translation are acceptable as corrections to reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of legitimate priority claim on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim under the Treaty is legitimate, the same invention as the invention described in the first application shall retain the same filing date as the filing date of the first application in accordance with Articles 29, 36 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any invention excluded in the first application shall not take the same filing date even if the priority claim is valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of priority effect for disclosure-exception timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain cases, the filing date of an application claiming priority shall be deemed to be the actual filing date; e.g., for applying the disclosure-exception provisions, if the applicant did not file within twelve months of disclosure, novelty or inventive step may be lost even if application was filed within one year from the first filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical warning that other timing rules (like disclosure exceptions) can make the effective filing date the actual filing date for some analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed period for amendment/addition/withdrawal of priority claims (1 year 4 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period allowed for amendment or addition of priority claim is within one year and four months from the earliest priority date. The designated time period for multiple priority claims containing a Domestic Priority claim is also one year and four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When additional priority claims are added or withdrawn, earliest priority date is recalculated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirement to amend/add priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: To amend or add a priority claim, an applicant shall have made a priority claim at the time of filing an application and at least one of the priority claims made at filing shall meet the requirement specified in Article 54(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an applicant has made a priority claim is determined by the indication in the 【Priority Claim】 column of the written application at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncorrectable errors in defective priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a priority claim under the Treaty does not fulfill the requirements specified in Article 54(1) and (2) of the Patent Act, the priority claim shall be deemed to have uncorrectable errors; amendments or addition of such a priority claim shall not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothetical, unspecified, or unidentifiable first applications cannot be corrected or added later.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amendments/additions are barred (withdrawn/invalidated/final decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim has been withdrawn or invalidated, or an application claiming priority has been invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned, or a decision to grant/reject becomes final and conclusive, the applicant shall not be able to amend or add the priority claim. After withdrawal of all priority claims, amendment/addition is not allowed, except adding a priority claim made on the same date as the withdrawal is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finality defined: decision to grant becomes final when certified copy of grant is served; decision to reject becomes final when thirty days have elapsed from service of certified copy of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted corrections within one year and four months without separate withdrawal document
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year and four months from the earliest filing date, withdrawal of all priority claims, withdrawal of part of priority claims in multiple priority claims, correction of clerical errors in priority claims, and addition of priority claims shall be permitted; applicants need not submit a separate withdrawal document and may submit an amendment reflecting the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifies procedural formality: use amendment to reflect withdrawal/addition/corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-deadline amendment restriction (only clerical corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments of a priority claim after one year and four months has elapsed shall be permitted only when correcting clerical errors in the indication of the priority claim. Amendments changing/specifying/adding the first application are not allowed. Withdrawal of all or part of priority claims is still allowed after the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limit after the 1y4m window; substantive changes barred, clerical corrections allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of formalities and substantive effects of prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an application claiming priority or a written amendment to priority is submitted, the examiner shall examine the formalities of the priority claim; unless any deficiency is found in the priority claim, the examiner shall carry out the substantive examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art search in substantive exam reveals no prior art between the filing date of the first application and the filing date of the application claiming priority, the examiner shall examine patentability based on the filing date of the first application. If prior art exists between those dates, the examiner shall examine whether the invention was described in the first application (and can request evidential documents/translations etc.).
